cover_hook: A 'lost' bird was filmed for the 1st time ever
caption_hook: 🐦 A 'lost' bird nobody had photographed in 13 years was just filmed for the first time in Côte d'Ivoire + 3 more wins 👇
question: Lost bird or 1,000-year-old mummies: which find would you rather make?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves birds

first_comment: Bonus: before the trip, the two bird surveyors joked about finding a 'lost' bird, knowing the odds were tiny. One of them got a photo before she even saw it. Ever had luck like that?

stories.headline: A bird lost for 13 years is filmed for the first time
stories.summary: Crossing a small rainforest bridge, two bird surveyors spotted a yellow, orange and black Ghana cuckooshrike, unseen since 2013, and took the first known video of it on a 6-month West Africa trip.
stories.why: Experts say the photos may be the best ever taken of this bird.

stories.headline: 4 mummies untouched for 1,000+ years rethink a conquest
stories.summary: In southern Peru, archaeologists found four Nasca mummies buried beside a Wari temple, not in the cemetery, with local food, pottery and alpaca offerings, hinting the 2 cultures worked together.
stories.why: An intact tomb is rare in Peru, and it hints an empire grew through teamwork, not just war.

stories.headline: A fabric born from army uniform research triples strawberries
stories.summary: NC State's 'Plant Armor' cover keeps bugs off plants but lets sun, rain and air through. Covered strawberries gave up to 3.56 times more fruit in tunnel field tests, and it kept out every aphid in lab tests.
stories.why: Fewer bugs without spraying could mean bigger harvests with less pesticide.

stories.headline: Stem-cell heart patches reach their 1st patient after approval
stories.summary: Surgeons in Japan placed sheets of heart muscle cells made from iPS stem cells on the heart of a woman in her 50s, the world's first surgery using the newly approved, commercially made sheets.
stories.why: Stem-cell science behind a 2012 Nobel Prize is now reaching people with failing hearts.

fun_fact: A bird species counts as 'lost' when no one has confirmed seeing it for at least 10 years.
